- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; increase forecast to align with recent upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next period; cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 5–10 day average, consider mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 1–2% to match historical volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action (last 7–10 days); apply a 1–3% upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to catch momentum — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
